# Phase 13 gate report: powering Phase 12's multi-hop test

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

[Phase 12](PHASE_12.md) found Quest-style selection losing much more on RULER variable tracking than
on the single needle at its two tightest budgets, but at 30 prompts per task its pre-committed test
(disjoint paired 95% CIs) could not separate the gap at 32K at either budget. This phase is Phase
9's remedy applied to Phase 12: more paired prompts, the rule unchanged and fixed before the run.

## Gate checklist (CLAUDE.md rule 3)

- [x] **Tests run.** `pytest`, all passing. New: the pooling guard (`analyze_phase13.py` refuses to
  pool two runs that answered any shared prompt differently).
- [x] **Real experiment run.** `scripts/02_policy_quality.py --config configs/phase13.yaml
  --sample-start 5`, detached from a worktree pinned at the commit under test.
- [x] **Phase doc written.** This file.
- [x] **Committed and pushed.**

## Design

At 32,768 tokens, Quest-style selection at 12.5% and 6.25%, on
variable tracking and the single needle: Phase 12's samples 0-4 pooled with this run's 5-29, which
is 150 prompts per task. Sample 5 ran in both
phases as a reproducibility check, and all
30 overlapping answers came back identical
(30 of
30), so the pooled set is one measurement. The
analysis imports Phase 12's functions rather than re-implementing them, so the rule applied is
literally the one Phase 12 committed.

## 1. The answer

| Budget | Single needle retention [95% CI] | Variable tracking retention [95% CI] | Pre-committed test | Difference CI (Phase 12's post-hoc test) |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 12.5% | 81.3% [74.7%–87.3%] | 69.4% [62.5%–76.2%] | **not established** | -21.1 pp to -2.6 pp |
| 6.25% | 61.3% [53.3%–68.7%] | 41.5% [35.4%–47.8%] | **established** | -29.6 pp to -9.9 pp |

**At 6.25% the shortfall is established.** With five times the prompts, the two intervals no longer
overlap, which Phase 12's 30 prompts at this context could not show.

**At 12.5% it is not, by the pre-committed rule.** The two intervals still overlap. The difference CI
excludes zero, but that test was introduced after Phase 12's data was read, and this phase does not
promote it to the rule after the fact. The honest statement is that a shortfall at 12.5% is likely
and not established.

**The effect is smaller than Phase 12 estimated.** At 30 prompts, Phase 12 put the 32K gap at
-23.8 pp (12.5%) and
-27.3 pp (6.25%); at
150 prompts it is
-11.9 pp and
-19.8 pp. Small samples overstate effects that clear a
bar, and this is that shrinkage. [Phase 12](PHASE_12.md)'s 32K numbers should be read through this
table.

Scored all-or-nothing (Phase 12's post-hoc view), Quest-style selection completes the whole chain on
46.0% (12.5%) and
14.3% (6.25%) of
the prompts the full cache solves.
